name: Arbutus

project_scope.note: Single-species genus study lesson uses identified neighboring taxa as references, not learner-approved new species. No new canonical species or nativity changes.

genus_recognition.look_here_first: Mature Texas madrone has dramatically peeling outer bark exposing smooth cream/pink/salmon/orange inner bark. Pair it with simple leathery evergreen leaves, pale URN-shaped flower clusters and orange/red berry-like fruit; never diagnose a seedling from bark alone.
genus_recognition.source_order: habit → leaf/stem architecture → flower structure → fruit/seed → specialist comparison

morphological_comparison_matrix.Arbutus xalapensis: smooth exfoliating multi-colored trunk/limbs in mature plants
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Vaccinium arboreum lacks this characteristic dramatic madrone bark; Diospyros older bark may peel in plates differently

morphological_comparison_matrix.Arbutus xalapensis: simple alternate leathery evergreen blade, often entire or toothed
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Vaccinium may have smaller narrower evergreen/semi-evergreen leaves; use flower and bark

morphological_comparison_matrix.Arbutus xalapensis: drooping pale urn-shaped (urceolate) flowers clustered on branch ends
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Vaccinium also urn-like; Diospyros tubular separate family and anther characters

morphological_comparison_matrix.Arbutus xalapensis: poricidal anthers opening via terminal pores, characteristic Ericaceae
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Diospyros not Ericaceae; examine flower section/anther tips

morphological_comparison_matrix.Arbutus xalapensis: round fleshy orange-red berry-like fruit in clusters
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Vaccinium fruit usually dark/black at maturity, other planted Arbutus may red; fruit color not alone

morphological_comparison_matrix.Arbutus xalapensis: wild Hill Country canyon/rocky woodland and sometimes nurse-tree associations
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: A. unedo landscape planting; provenance and age required to use bark/habitat

visual_id_sequence: 1. Inspect entire plant habit and growth form.
2. Zoom to stem node and complete mature leaf with ruler.
3. Inspect close flower and reproductive parts, labeling all structures rather than flower color alone.
4. Confirm mature fruit architecture with macro and seed view.
5. Compare the nearest confuser against matched structural photos; keep ambiguous IDs at genus.

diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: old trunk bark with scale and exfoliating outer layer
young twig and mature leaf underside with venation
pale urn-shaped open flowers and closed buds
dissected flower with pores at anther tips
young vs ripe fruit with leaf context
